prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
At Mazda Stadium on August 16, 2026, Hanshin took control before Hiroshima could settle in.

In the first inning, Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field. Hanshin quickly took the lead.

Hanshin also had a strong foundation on the mound. Starting pitcher Rihito Ihara worked five innings, allowed only two hits, and gave up one run.

That run came in the fifth inning. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run for Hiroshima. It was the Carp’s only score.

Hanshin did not let that moment change the result. The Tigers added runs in the seventh and eighth innings, and the gap continued to grow.

The final score was Hiroshima 1, Hanshin 8.

It was a complete Hanshin victory. Sato created the early advantage, Ihara limited Hiroshima’s scoring, and the team finished by making its lead even bigger.

【Point One】
The late cushion had more than one source. Seishiro Sakamoto drove in a run in the seventh, then hit a run-scoring double in the eighth. Tora Fushimi also drove in a run as a pinch-hitter. The final margin came from several contributions, not just one early swing.

【Point Two】
Montero’s fifth-inning home run should be read carefully. It was Hiroshima’s only run, and no more followed. The record shows an isolated scoring moment. It does not confirm that the home run changed momentum, lifted the home team, or started a comeback. That distinction keeps the story tied to what the game actually showed.
